newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar called to open 0.05 cent higher.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar called to open 0.05 cent higher.

text.p: CSCE world sugar was called to open 0.05 cent firmer Monday in response to sharply higher prices in London, dealers said.

Fears of a shortage of sugar in August, a time of transition between crops, brought out mixed buying and lifted benchmark LIFFE August to an intraday high of $315.10. At 0840 EDT/1340 GMT, the contract stood at $314.90, up $1.60, with back months were $1.10 higher to down $0.70.
USDA approved a 200,000 tonne increase in the U.S. sugar import quota, and forecast a 1996/97 sugar stocks-to-use ratio of 15.4 percent. The ratio is a key figure in setting the import quota.

USDA allocated 1.7 million tonnes of sugar imports at the beginning of fiscal 1997, but said adjustments would be considered during the year. A ratio of 15.5 percent or less boosts the quota by 200,000 tonnes.

CFTC's Commitments of Traders report for the two weeks ended May 6 showed noncommercial long positions fell by 7,772 lots, to 40,828 lots, while noncommerial short positions fell by 1,5571lots to 2,850 lots.
Commercial long positions in the two weeks fell by 7,959 lots, to 55,228 lots, and commerial short positions fell by 16,427 lots to 113,239 lots.
Non-reportable long positions fell by 7,948 lots, to 46,927 lots, while nonreportable short positions fell by 5,671 lots to 26,894 lots.
Friday, most-active CSCE July closed 0.04 cent firmer at 10.88 cents per lb after trading from 10.89 to 10.77 cents. The rest of the board settled 0.01 higher to down 0.03.
For July delivery, support remained at Thursday's low of 10.73 cents followed by 10.65 cents, the recent low reached on May 2. Resistance remained at 10.92 cents.
((-- S Rostler New York Commodity Desk, 212-859-1640))
